name: fastsnap
summary: A second, faster reset path beside savevm/loadvm, for fuzzing. Device state goes into one heap buffer (adopted); RAM is restored per dirty page through QEMU's own migration bitmap (ours); a forked child read back with process_vm_readv is the correctness oracle (ours). Measured at 348-560 us per reset, verified byte-identical to the oracle across 281-403 MB of guest RAM.
notes:
The adopted code is whole files under srcPaths, never interleaved into patch hunks, and it is the DEVICE half only. The RAM half is ours and deliberately uses QEMU's DIRTY_MEMORY_MIGRATION bitmap rather than the upstream project's own write hooks, which self-disarm on a warm guest: TCG traps a store only while TLB_NOTDIRTY is set, notdirty_write() clears it on the first write, and nothing there re-arms it -- so its dirty list comes back plausibly small and the restore is silently incomplete. Measured: 0/64 pages trapped after a mid-run snapshot point, 64/64 once tracking is re-armed.

Neither half is sound alone. Restoring devices without RAM rewinds the CPU's page-table base into RAM that was never rewound; on real firmware that destroys the guest within a handful of restores (kernel panic in rcu_process_callbacks, swap_dup errors, OOM kills) while an identical cadence with the restore removed stays clean.

The series patches are ours. 0014 adds accessors to migration/savevm.c so the adopted code never sees SaveStateEntry's layout -- deliberately NOT the struct hoist the upstream project uses. 0015-0017 are a bug fix and two save-side costs found by profiling the round trip.
